test_title: PYST 35: RRB NTPC Graduate Level CBT-I - GA (Held On: 19 Jun, 2025 Shift 3)
subject: general
question: The Northern Plains of India have been primarily formed by which of the following processes?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Deposition of alluvium**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Northern Plains of India were formed due to the **deposition of alluvial soil brought by the rivers** originating from the Himalayas and the Peninsular Plateau.
 
• The plains are composed of layers of **fine silt, sand, and clay** deposited over millions of years.
 
• The three major Himalayan rivers—**the Ganga, the Brahmaputra, and the Indus**—along with their tributaries, played a crucial role in shaping these fertile plains.
 
• This region is known for its **fertile soil**, making it one of the most agriculturally productive areas in India.
 
• The Northern Plains are categorized into three sections—**the Bhabar, the Terai, and the Alluvial Plains** (Khadar and Bangar).

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Alluvium:**

 
 
• Alluvium refers to the **fine-grained fertile soil** deposited by rivers over time.
 
• This type of soil is rich in minerals and nutrients, making it suitable for agriculture.
 
 
 
• **Himalayan Rivers:**
 
 
• The rivers originating from the Himalayas, such as the Ganga, Brahmaputra, and Indus, are **perennial**, meaning they flow throughout the year.
 
• These rivers are fed by **glacial melt** and monsoon rains.
 
 
 
• **Bhabar and Terai:**
 
 
• **Bhabar:** A narrow belt of coarse gravel and pebbles found at the foothills of the Himalayas.
 
• **Terai:** A marshy and swampy region south of the Bhabar, characterized by dense vegetation.
 
 
 
• **Khadar and Bangar:**
 
 
• **Khadar:** The newer, fertile alluvial soil found in the river's floodplains.
 
• **Bangar:** The older alluvial soil found further away from the riverbanks, less fertile than Khadar.
 
 
 
• **Agricultural Significance:**
 
 
• The Northern Plains are often referred to as the "Granary of India" due to their high agricultural output.
 
• Main crops grown in the region include wheat, rice, sugarcane, and pulses.
